title: Introduction to MAGICR
text: MAGICR native R implementation MAGIC (Markov Affinity-based Graph Imputation Cells) algorithm denoising imputation single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. Single-cell RNA sequencing revolutionized understanding cellular heterogeneity, technical limitations result sparse count matrices prevalent dropout events—expressed genes appear zeros due sampling inefficiency. MAGIC addresses challenge leveraging underlying manifold structure data diffusion geometry.

title: MAGIC Algorithm: Mathematical Foundations
text: vignette provides comprehensive mathematical description MAGIC algorithm. Understanding foundations helps users make informed decisions parameter selection interpret results correctly.

title: MAGIC Algorithm: Mathematical Foundations
text: Single-cell RNA sequencing captures transcriptomic profiles single-cell resolution, suffers technical limitations: Low capture efficiency: 10-20% mRNA molecules captured Amplification bias: PCR amplification introduces noise Dropout events: Expressed genes appear zeros due sampling issues result sparse, noisy count matrices biological signal obscured.

title: MAGIC Algorithm: Mathematical Foundations
text: MAGIC leverages manifold hypothesis: high-dimensional single-cell data lies lower-dimensional manifold reflecting biological states. diffusing information along manifold, MAGIC recovers missing transcripts preserving biological structure.

title: MAGIC Algorithm: Mathematical Foundations
text: computational efficiency, MAGIC first reduces dimensionality using PCA: Xpca=X⋅VkX_{pca} = X \cdot V_k VkV_k contains top kk principal components (default: 100).

title: MAGIC Algorithm: Mathematical Foundations
text: cell ii, identify kk nearest neighbors based Euclidean distance PCA space: 𝒩k()={j:d(xi,xj)≤dk(xi)}\mathcal{N}_k() = \{j : d(x_i, x_j) \leq d_k(x_i)\} dk(xi)d_k(x_i) distance kk-th nearest neighbor.

title: MAGIC Algorithm: Mathematical Foundations
text: affinity cells computed using α-decaying kernel adaptive bandwidth: K(xi,xj)=exp⁡(−(∥xi−xj∥2εi)α)K(x_i, x_j) = \exp\left(-\left(\frac{\|x_i - x_j\|_2}{\varepsilon_i}\right)^\alpha\right) : εi=dk(xi)\varepsilon_i = d_k(x_i) adaptive bandwidth (distance kk-th neighbor) α\alpha controls kernel sharpness (default: 1) adaptive bandwidth? Accounts varying local density Cells dense regions smaller bandwidth Cells sparse regions larger bandwidth Preserves rare cell populations
code: # Visualize α-decaying kernel x <- seq(0, 3, length.out = 100)  par(mfrow = c(1, 2))  # Effect of distance plot(x, exp(-x), type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#e74c3c",      xlab = "Normalized Distance (d/ε)", ylab = "Affinity K(x,y)",      main = "α-Decaying Kernel (α = 1)") abline(h = 0.5, lty = 2, col = "gray") abline(v = log(2), lty = 2, col = "gray")  # Effect of α plot(x, exp(-x^0.5), type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "#3498db",      xlab = "Normalized Distance (d/ε)", ylab = "Affinity K(x,y)",      main = "Effect of α Parameter", ylim = c(0, 1)) lines(x, exp(-x^1), lwd = 2, col = "#e74c3c") lines(x, exp(-x^2), lwd = 2, col = "#2ecc71") legend("topright", legend = c("α = 0.5", "α = 1", "α = 2"),        col = c("#3498db", "#e74c3c", "#2ecc71"), lwd = 2)

title: MAGIC Algorithm: Mathematical Foundations
text: kernel matrix row-normalized create Markov transition matrix: P=D−1KP = D^{-1}K DD diagonal degree matrix Dii=∑jKijD_{ii} = \sum_j K_{ij}. Properties P: Row-stochastic: ∑jPij=1\sum_j P_{ij} = 1 Represents transition probabilities random walk Eigenvalues [−1,1][-1, 1]

title: MAGIC Algorithm: Mathematical Foundations
text: diffusion operator powered tt times: Ximputed=PtXX_{imputed} = P^t X power PP propagates information one step along graph: t=1t = 1: Local averaging immediate neighbors t=2t = 2: Information 2-hop neighbors t=tt = t: Information tt-hop neighborhood
code: # Simulate diffusion effect set.seed(42) n <- 100 x <- c(rnorm(50, -2, 0.5), rnorm(50, 2, 0.5)) y <- c(rnorm(50, 0, 0.5), rnorm(50, 0, 0.5))  # Add noise x_noisy <- x + rnorm(n, 0, 0.3) y_noisy <- y + rnorm(n, 0, 0.3)  par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) plot(x_noisy, y_noisy, pch = 16, col = adjustcolor("#3498db", 0.6),      main = "Before Diffusion (Noisy)", xlab = "Gene 1", ylab = "Gene 2")  # Simple smoothing simulation x_smooth <- 0.7 * x + 0.3 * x_noisy y_smooth <- 0.7 * y + 0.3 * y_noisy plot(x_smooth, y_smooth, pch = 16, col = adjustcolor("#e74c3c", 0.6),      main = "After Diffusion (Denoised)", xlab = "Gene 1", ylab = "Gene 2")

title: MAGIC Algorithm: Mathematical Foundations
text: t = "auto", MAGIC uses Procrustes analysis find optimal diffusion time.

title: MAGIC Algorithm: Mathematical Foundations
text: Given two matrices XX YY, Procrustes analysis finds optimal rotation RR minimizes: dProcrustes(X,Y)=∥X−YR∥F2d_{Procrustes}(X, Y) = \|X - YR\|_F^2 centering normalizing matrices.

title: MAGIC Algorithm: Mathematical Foundations
text: MAGIC iteratively applies diffusion monitors: Δt=dProcrustes(Xt,Xt+1)\Delta_t = d_{Procrustes}(X_t, X_{t+1}) algorithm stops Δt<θ\Delta_t < \theta (default: 0.001), indicating convergence.
code: library(MAGICR) data(magic_testdata)  # Run with automatic t selection result <- magic(magic_testdata, t = "auto", t_max = 15, verbose = TRUE)  cat("\nOptimal t selected:", result$params$t, "\n") #>  #> Optimal t selected: 15

title: MAGIC Algorithm: Mathematical Foundations
text: Computes imputation full gene space: Ximputed=PtXX_{imputed} = P^t X Advantages: - Preserves gene-gene relationships - approximation error Disadvantages: - Memory intensive large gene sets - Slower computation

title: MAGIC Algorithm: Mathematical Foundations
text: Operates PCA space projects back: Ximputed=PtXpca⋅VkTX_{imputed} = P^t X_{pca} \cdot V_k^T Advantages: - Much faster large datasets - Lower memory footprint Disadvantages: - information loss PCA projection

title: MAGIC Algorithm: Mathematical Foundations
text: diffusion process elegant spectral interpretation. PP eigendecomposition: P=∑iλiviviTP = \sum_i \lambda_i v_i v_i^T : Pt=∑iλitviviTP^t = \sum_i \lambda_i^t v_i v_i^T Since |λi|≤1|\lambda_i| \leq 1: Small eigenvalues (high-frequency noise) decay rapidly Large eigenvalues (low-frequency signal) persist Diffusion acts low-pass filter

title: Integration with Seurat
text: MAGICR provides seamless integration Seurat objects, supporting Seurat v4 v5. vignette demonstrates use MAGIC within typical Seurat workflow.

title: Integration with Seurat
code: # Install required packages install.packages("Seurat") install.packages("MAGICR", repos = "https://zaoqu-liu.r-universe.dev")

title: Integration with Seurat
code: library(Seurat) library(MAGICR)  # Create example Seurat object # In practice, load your own data data(magic_testdata) seurat_obj <- CreateSeuratObject(counts = t(magic_testdata))

title: Integration with Seurat
code: # Normalize data seurat_obj <- NormalizeData(seurat_obj)  # Find variable features seurat_obj <- FindVariableFeatures(seurat_obj, nfeatures = 2000)  # Scale data seurat_obj <- ScaleData(seurat_obj)  # Run PCA seurat_obj <- RunPCA(seurat_obj, npcs = 50)

title: Integration with Seurat
code: # Run MAGIC on the Seurat object seurat_obj <- magic(seurat_obj,                      assay = "RNA",                     t = 3,                     knn = 5)  # MAGIC results are stored in a new assay Assays(seurat_obj)

code: # Switch to MAGIC assay for downstream analysis DefaultAssay(seurat_obj) <- "MAGIC_RNA"  # Get imputed expression matrix magic_data <- GetAssayData(seurat_obj, assay = "MAGIC_RNA", layer = "data")

title: MAGICR - Markov Affinity-based Graph Imputation of Cells
text: MAGICR native R implementation MAGIC (Markov Affinity-based Graph Imputation Cells) algorithm denoising imputation single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data. Single-cell RNA sequencing enables transcriptomic profiling single-cell resolution, technical limitations result sparse count matrices prevalent dropout events. MAGIC addresses challenge leveraging underlying manifold structure data diffusion geometry, effectively recovering missing transcripts preserving biological signal.

title: MAGICR - Markov Affinity-based Graph Imputation of Cells
text: MAGIC performs data imputation following steps: Dimensionality Reduction: Optional PCA reduce computational complexity Graph Construction: Build k-nearest neighbor (kNN) graph based cell-cell distances Kernel Computation: Construct α-decaying kernel adaptive bandwidth: K(xi,xj)=exp⁡(−(∥xi−xj∥2εi)α)K(x_i, x_j) = \exp\left(-\left(\frac{\|x_i - x_j\|_2}{\varepsilon_i}\right)^\alpha\right) εi\varepsilon_i distance kk-th nearest neighbor cell ii. Diffusion Operator: Compute row-stochastic Markov transition matrix: P=D−1KP = D^{-1}K Imputation: Apply powered diffusion: Ximputed=PtXX_{\text{imputed}} = P^t X diffusion time tt controls degree smoothing. t = "auto", optimal tt selected minimizing Procrustes disparity successive iterations.
